evidence: epel-release-installed: manifests/extra_packages_el.pp:6-10 runs dnf install of epel-release-latest-${os_major_version}.noarch.rpm guarded by rpm -q epel-release; on the RHEL 9.5 node that yields epel-release version 9, and the probe expects exactly 'epel-release 9' plus the epel repo enabled (the release package ships epel.repo enabled). Failed clean, passed applied in my run.

baseos-appstream-still-enabled: lines 13-16 only run subscription-manager repos --enable for codeready-builder-for-rhel-9-x86_64-rpms (unless grep on --list-enabled); nothing in the class disables a repository, so BaseOS and AppStream enabled at the registered baseline must stay enabled. why_invariant is plausible; passed on both clean and applied node.

an-epel-package-installs-from-epel: lines 6-11 make EPEL the source the class exists for; the action (dnf install htop, output discarded) is a consumer use of that repo, and the read-only effect (repoquery --installed from_repo) shows the result, not the action's output. htop is EPEL-only on RHEL 9 (dnf history on the node: htop-3.3.0-1.el9 @epel). mutates says 'installs htop with dnf'; dnf also pulled hwloc-libs from BaseOS (and ninja-build pulled emacs-filesystem/vim-filesystem) as normal dependency resolution of that install, on a node reverted after every run.

purpose covered: Purpose (EPEL for the node's major version and CodeReady Builder enabled so packages from either install, base repos untouched) matches the whole 21-line baseline manifest and its two header comments (lines 6, 13). Checks test it as behaviour, not just state: epel-release 9 installed + epel repo enabled, CRB enabled in subscription-manager and dnf, an EPEL-only package (htop) and a CRB package (ninja-build) actually install with dnf recording epel / codeready-builder-for-rhel-9-x86_64-rpms as source, and BaseOS/AppStream still enabled. The EPEL-before-CRB require ordering has no separate observable outcome. Left out: RHEL 8 (lines 3-4 derive the version from facts), honestly uncovered because nodes.yml has no RHEL 8 kind; its lifted_by names rhel9 only because the validator requires an existing kind - the why states the truth. Other architectures than x86_64 are likewise not available in the lab.
